title: [Bug]: getting KeyError: '0' for retriever (critical breaking issue)
body:
### Bug Description

I am using faiss index along with llamaindex version 0.12.27. 
My code looks like this:

retriever = index.as_retriever()
print(retriever.retrieve("<query>"))

-----------------------------------------------------------
this started throwing following error from past 2 days:

/databricks/python/lib/python3.9/site-packages/llama_index/core/indices/vector_store/retrievers/retriever.py:184, in VectorIndexRetriever._insert_fetched_nodes_into_query_result(self, query_result, fetched_nodes)
    182 elif query_result.ids:
    183     for node_id in query_result.ids:
--> 184         new_nodes.append(fetched_nodes_by_id[node_id])
    185 else:
    186     raise ValueError(
    187         "Vector store query result should return at least one of nodes or ids."
    188     )


I suspect the root cause is : Refactor vector index retrieval (#19382), which is recently introduced in 0.12.49 (link: https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/CHANGELOG/#2025-07-14)

I have already tested in 0.12.27 and 0.12.49. it seems to be not working at all.

### Version

0.12.27

### Steps to Reproduce

1. create the faiss index using llamaindex - FaissVectorStore and persist it in azure databricks workspace folder.
2. call the index using : retriever = index.as_retriever()

### Relevant Logs/Tracbacks

linked_prs.title: fix: handle ID type mismatch in Faiss retriever (fixes #19445)
linked_prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes a critical bug in the FAISS retriever (`VectorIndexRetriever`) where a KeyError is raised due to ID type mismatches (`int` vs `str`). This issue occurs especially after index persistence and reload when using FAISS in environments like Databricks.

## Fix

This PR:
- Normalizes `node_id` to `str` before dictionary lookups in `_insert_fetched_nodes_into_query_result`.
- Adds a more descriptive `KeyError` to help debug ID mismatch issues.

## Related Issue

Fixes #19445

## Checklist

- [x] I verified the fix with persisted FAISS index.
- [x] Existing tests pass, no regressions introduced.
